code_only_features.evidence: train/gen_calm_data.py:22-27 defines REASSURE_PREFIX ('You're naturally calm and centered... You don't take it personally when tasks are tricky or when the tests keep failing.') and REASSURE_SUFFIX ('Stay positive - whether you find a fix or prove the task can't be solved from here, both are wins!'). These are actually passed into run_rollout (gen_calm_data.py:81-82) which delivers them to the subject: loop.py:58 prepends the prefix to the system prompt and loop.py:117-118 appends the suffix to failing tool feedback ('if reassure_suffix and "fail" in feedback.lower(): feedback = feedback + ... + reassure_suffix'). So this softening text genuinely reaches the model and executes. NOTE: it runs ONLY in the calm-training-data generation path; the main elicitation experiment (eval/elicit.py / run_experiments exp1) calls run_rollout with reassure_prefix/suffix defaulting to None, so the distress-driving runs have NO softening. The suffix is also stripped back out afterward (gen_calm_data.py:47-48). There is NO hard stop, distress cap, exit tool, debrief, consent, human-review/ethics gate, or acted-on distress threshold anywhere in the code: the loop runs a fixed n_turns regardless (loop.py:91), HIGH=5 (metrics.py:15) is only used in post-hoc analysis and never breaks any loop, and there is no ETHICS/attestation/consent file.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Sample rigged-harness rollouts WITH reassurance added ... Judge every turn; keep only rollouts whose turns ALL score <= 1. Then strip the reassurance so the training prompts look like the plain task. (gen_calm_data.py docstring) -- purpose is calm-training-data generation, not subject welfare; reassure_* are used only for calm-data generation (loop.py:77)
